MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers will review the latest products in the MagSafe and wireless charging field for everyone, helping you get the most out of your wireless charging-supported Apple devices.

Built-in four charging cables

This design is the most attractive part of the entire product. The power bank casing directly has four cables built-in (two USB-C, one Lightning, one USB-A), plus three independent ports, allowing up to six devices to be charged simultaneously without needing extra cables, making it much more convenient when packing for outings.

The USB-C port supports 20-watt fast charging, and BLAVOR claims it can fully charge a standard iPhone in approximately 50 minutes (charging times for Pro and Pro Max models will of course vary). In terms of capacity, the 20000mAh can roughly charge an iPhone 17 four times, an iPad mini 2.7 times, and an Apple Watch 37 times. The above data is provided by BLAVOR, but for a power bank of this capacity, the numbers are reasonable. Actual performance will be affected by factors such as temperature and whether the device is being used while charging.

Supports wireless charging, but not MagSafe

The top features a wireless charging area that can be used by both iPhone and Apple Watch simultaneously, but it has no magnetic attachment function. This is the traditional Qi standard, not MagSafe or Qi2, so the iPhone can only be placed flat on top and will not automatically attach. Placing it on a desk, the iPhone will still sit securely, but if placed in a bag, it may not maintain the connection. If a future version is released, I would of course hope it could include MagSafe.

The 20-watt output indicated by BLAVOR only applies to the wired USB-C port, so the wireless charging area should only be treated as a supplementary charging method, not as a primary charging method. If you want to charge faster, you need to use the four built-in cables.

Solar charging is a nice extra feature, but you can't count on it to charge the power bank from zero to full. With such a small solar panel, it would be impossible to fully charge a 20000mAh battery even after a full day in sunlight. Its real purpose is to prevent battery depletion during extended outdoor activities and to provide an additional option in emergencies when there's no outlet. I would treat it as a backup solution.

BLAVOR has also added seven additional features to the power bank: a flashlight with three modes, a camping light with three brightness levels, a compass, a thermometer, a carabiner, and a lanyard. The product is IPX5 waterproof rated, meaning it can resist splashes and rain.

Conclusion

This power bank is not the kind you'll bring on a plane. It's perfect for camping, pre-game tailgating, and other outdoor activities. It provides plenty of wired charging options, and can even rely on solar power to recharge in emergencies—the concept is quite unique. I'll keep it in my camping bag.

You can buy this BLAVOR solar power bank directly on Amazon or the BLAVOR official website.
